question.text: What do Florida-owned cars need, and how soon must newcomers register?

answer.text: An owned vehicle requires Florida registration, a license plate, and a Florida title unless held by an out-of-state lienholder; non-residents who start work or enroll children in Florida public school have ten days to register with Florida insurance and title proof, and out-of-state vehicles need vehicle identification number verification except new vehicles, new or used mobile homes, trailer-type recreational vehicles, and trailers or semitrailers under two thousand pounds.

teaching.text: Cars owned here need Florida registration, plates and a title, newcomers register within ten days, insurance and title prove ownership, and used cars from other states get a VIN check. Remember: Register, plate, title, ten days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An owned vehicle requires Florida registration, a license plate, and a Florida title unless held by an out-of-state lienholder; non-residents who start work or enroll children in Florida public school have ten days to register with Florida insurance and title proof, and out-of-state vehicles need vehicle identification number verification except new vehicles, new or used mobile homes, trailer-type recreational vehicles, and trailers or semitrailers under two thousand pounds.

question.text: How are titles and plates issued, and who files after a sale?

answer.text: Service centers title and plate by weight and type, plates stay current with papers aboard, dealers file for buyers while private buyers file themselves, titles precede plates, and out-of-state licensees license first.

teaching.text: Service centers issue titles and plates by weight and type, papers ride in the car, dealers file for their buyers, private buyers file for themselves, and the title always comes first. Remember: Title comes before plates.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Service centers title and plate by weight and type, plates stay current with papers aboard, dealers file for buyers while private buyers file themselves, titles precede plates, and out-of-state licensees license first.

question.text: When do registrations expire, and how early can they be renewed?

answer.text: Renewals run yearly or biennial to the birthday midnight, mobile homes and semis to December thirty-one, fleets to June thirty, open ninety days early, and recheck insurance.

teaching.text: Most registrations run one or two years to midnight on the owner's birthday, mobile homes and semis to the end of December, fleets to the end of June, and renewal opens ninety days early. Remember: Birthday midnight, ninety days early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Renewals run yearly or biennial to the birthday midnight, mobile homes and semis to December thirty-one, fleets to June thirty, open ninety days early, and recheck insurance.

question.text: What comes before plates, and how soon do newcomers file?

answer.text: You must hold a title proving ownership before getting a license plate, non-residents beginning Florida employment or public-school enrollment must register within ten days, and out-of-state vehicles require vehicle identification number verification except new vehicles, mobile homes, trailer-type recreational vehicles, and trailers or semitrailers weighing under two thousand pounds.

teaching.text: The title proves who owns the car and comes before any plate, newcomers have ten days to file, and used out-of-state cars get a VIN check. Remember: Prove ownership, then plate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must hold a title proving ownership before getting a license plate, non-residents beginning Florida employment or public-school enrollment must register within ten days, and out-of-state vehicles require vehicle identification number verification except new vehicles, mobile homes, trailer-type recreational vehicles, and trailers or semitrailers weighing under two thousand pounds.

question.text: How do renewal deadlines differ by vehicle type?

answer.text: Renewals die at the birthday midnight, mobile rigs at year end, fleets at midyear, and all reopen ninety days early.

teaching.text: Ordinary registrations end at the birthday midnight, mobile homes and semis at year end, fleets at midyear, and every renewal can start ninety days ahead. Remember: Birthday, year end, midyear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Renewals die at the birthday midnight, mobile rigs at year end, fleets at midyear, and all reopen ninety days early.

question.text: What equipment and lamp distances does every car need?

answer.text: Required gear spans dual brakes, low beams one hundred fifty ahead and one thousand seen, high beams four hundred fifty and one thousand, tails one thousand, brake lamps three hundred by day, plate lamps fifty, signals five hundred, horns two hundred, mirrors two hundred, wipers, plain safety glass, tint caps twenty-five and thirty-five, and three thirty-seconds tread.

teaching.text: Every car needs dual brakes, working lamps that meet set distances, signals, a horn, mirrors, wipers, plain safety glass, legal tint and enough tread. Remember: Lights, brakes, horn, mirrors, wipers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Required gear spans dual brakes, low beams one hundred fifty ahead and one thousand seen, high beams four hundred fifty and one thousand, tails one thousand, brake lamps three hundred by day, plate lamps fifty, signals five hundred, horns two hundred, mirrors two hundred, wipers, plain safety glass, tint caps twenty-five and thirty-five, and three thirty-seconds tread.

question.text: Which vehicle equipment is banned?

answer.text: Prohibited vehicle equipment includes red lights visible from ahead, blue lights, more than two spotlights, fender, cowl, fog, or other extra lights, sirens, bells, or whistles, mufflers emitting smoke or audible beyond fifty feet, and signs, posters, or stickers on windshields or windows unless required by law.

teaching.text: Forward red or blue lamps, three extra lamps, sirens and bells, mufflers that are loud or smoke past fifty feet, and stickers on the glass are all banned. Remember: No red or blue up front.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Prohibited vehicle equipment includes red lights visible from ahead, blue lights, more than two spotlights, fender, cowl, fog, or other extra lights, sirens, bells, or whistles, mufflers emitting smoke or audible beyond fifty feet, and signs, posters, or stickers on windshields or windows unless required by law.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: No red or blue up front

question.text: What else is banned in the cabin, and what do airbags do?

answer.text: Driver-visible television and worn headsets are also banned, manuals answer car-specific questions, and airbags assist rather than replace belts.

teaching.text: Screens the driver can see and headsets worn while driving are banned, the owner's manual explains your car's features, and airbags only add to the seat belt. Remember: Airbags assist, belts protect.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driver-visible television and worn headsets are also banned, manuals answer car-specific questions, and airbags assist rather than replace belts.

question.text: How do low beam, high beam and other lamp distances compare?

answer.text: Low beams show one hundred fifty and high beams four hundred fifty, both seen at one thousand, tails at one thousand, brake lamps three hundred by day, and plates fifty.

teaching.text: Low beams light one hundred fifty ahead and high beams four hundred fifty, both visible at one thousand, with tail lamps at one thousand, brake lamps at three hundred and plate lamps at fifty. Remember: Low one-fifty, high four-fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Low beams show one hundred fifty and high beams four hundred fifty, both seen at one thousand, tails at one thousand, brake lamps three hundred by day, and plates fifty.

question.text: Which vehicle lights, noisemakers, mufflers, and glass items are prohibited?

answer.text: Forward-visible red lights, blue lights, more than two extra lights, sirens, bells, or whistles, smoking or loud mufflers heard past fifty feet, and window or windshield signs, posters, or stickers not required by law are prohibited equipment.

teaching.text: Forward red or blue lamps, a third extra light, noisemakers, loud mufflers and glass stickers all cause a car to fail inspection. Remember: No sirens or unlawful stickers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Forward-visible red lights, blue lights, more than two extra lights, sirens, bells, or whistles, smoking or loud mufflers heard past fifty feet, and window or windshield signs, posters, or stickers not required by law are prohibited equipment.

question.text: Why are screens and headsets banned, and can airbags replace belts?

answer.text: Screens and headsets distract illegally while airbags only assist belts, never replacing them.

teaching.text: Screens and headsets are banned because they distract the driver, and airbags help the belt but can never take its place. Remember: Screens distract, airbags only assist.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Screens and headsets distract illegally while airbags only assist belts, never replacing them.

question.text: What do warning-only assistance systems do?

answer.text: Warning-only helpers flag blind spots, closing gaps, lane drift, and reverse cross traffic without ever acting.

teaching.text: Warning-only systems tell you about blind spots, closing gaps, lane drift and cross traffic behind you, but they never take action themselves. Remember: They warn but never act.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Warning-only helpers flag blind spots, closing gaps, lane drift, and reverse cross traffic without ever acting.

question.text: What do acting assistance systems do?

answer.text: Acting helpers brake for frontal and pedestrian crashes and nudge back drifting lane changers.

teaching.text: Acting systems step in by braking to help prevent frontal and pedestrian crashes and by nudging back a car that drifts during a lane change. Remember: Brakes for you, steers back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Acting helpers brake for frontal and pedestrian crashes and nudge back drifting lane changers.

question.text: What do reverse braking, adaptive cruise and lane aids do?

answer.text: Reverse braking guards backing, adaptive cruise spaces the gap, centering holds the middle, and keeping corrects straying wheels.

teaching.text: Reverse braking protects you while backing, adaptive cruise keeps a gap, lane centering holds the middle, and lane keeping corrects wheels that stray. Remember: Controls differ by system.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reverse braking guards backing, adaptive cruise spaces the gap, centering holds the middle, and keeping corrects straying wheels.

question.text: What do crash callers, automatic beams and backup cameras do?

answer.text: Crash callers summon rescuers, auto beams swap with traffic, and backup cameras never replace mirrors and head turns.

teaching.text: Crash-calling systems contact rescuers, automatic beams switch with traffic, and a backup camera never replaces using mirrors and turning your head. Remember: Cameras never replace head turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crash callers summon rescuers, auto beams swap with traffic, and backup cameras never replace mirrors and head turns.

question.text: How do warning helpers differ from acting helpers?

answer.text: Warning helpers only alert on spots, gaps, drift, and cross traffic, while acting helpers brake and steer back.

teaching.text: Warning systems only alert you to a blind spot, a closing gap, drift or cross traffic, while acting systems actually brake or steer the car back. Remember: Alert only versus brake and steer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Warning helpers only alert on spots, gaps, drift, and cross traffic, while acting helpers brake and steer back.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Alert only versus brake and steer

question.text: What does each automated driving aid control?

answer.text: Rear automatic braking can stop a reversing vehicle. Adaptive cruise changes speed to maintain a selected gap. Lane centering makes continuous steering adjustments, while lane keeping may steer, brake or accelerate individual wheels, or combine these actions, to guide the vehicle back into its lane.

teaching.text: Lane centering steers continuously, while lane keeping may combine steering, braking or acceleration to return the vehicle to its lane. Remember: Lane keeping can combine controls.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rear automatic braking can stop a reversing vehicle. Adaptive cruise changes speed to maintain a selected gap. Lane centering makes continuous steering adjustments, while lane keeping may steer, brake or accelerate individual wheels, or combine these actions, to guide the vehicle back into its lane.

question.text: Can a backup camera replace mirrors and looking back?

answer.text: Crash callers phone rescuers, auto beams swap for traffic, and cameras never replace mirrors and looks.

teaching.text: A crash caller phones for help, automatic beams switch for other traffic, and no camera ever replaces your mirrors and your own look back. Remember: Still check mirrors and look.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crash callers phone rescuers, auto beams swap for traffic, and cameras never replace mirrors and looks.

question.text: How should you brake hard with anti-lock brakes?

answer.text: Anti-lock drivers stomp, hold, and steer while electronics pump faster, and pumping or lifting kills the assist.

teaching.text: With anti-lock brakes, press hard, keep holding and steer while the system pumps faster than you could, because pumping or lifting cancels its help. Remember: Stomp, hold, steer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anti-lock drivers stomp, hold, and steer while electronics pump faster, and pumping or lifting kills the assist.

question.text: How do you stop with plain brakes, and what body rules apply?

answer.text: Plain-brake drivers pump sliding stops, bumper heights step twenty-two through thirty inches by car and truck weight, and emission tampering is illegal.

teaching.text: With plain brakes, pump the pedal to stop a slide; bumper heights rise from twenty-two to thirty inches with vehicle weight, and tampering with emissions equipment is illegal. Remember: Pump plain brakes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Plain-brake drivers pump sliding stops, bumper heights step twenty-two through thirty inches by car and truck weight, and emission tampering is illegal.

question.text: What lighting do light and heavy trailers need?

answer.text: Light trailers need twin reflectors plus a brake lamp when hidden, while heavy ones add clearance and marker lamps with rear reflectors.

teaching.text: A light trailer needs two reflectors and a brake lamp when its lamps are hidden, while a heavy trailer adds clearance and marker lamps with rear reflectors. Remember: Heavy trailers add lamps.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Light trailers need twin reflectors plus a brake lamp when hidden, while heavy ones add clearance and marker lamps with rear reflectors.

question.text: What kills the anti-lock assist during a hard stop?

answer.text: Anti-lock stops stomp, hold, and steer, and any pumping or lifting kills the assist.

teaching.text: In an anti-lock stop, press firmly, hold and steer, because pumping or lifting the pedal shuts off the anti-lock help. Remember: Never pump anti-lock brakes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anti-lock stops stomp, hold, and steer, and any pumping or lifting kills the assist.

question.text: How do plain-brake stops, bumper heights and emission rules work?

answer.text: Plain brakes pump sliding stops, bumpers step with weight, and emission tampering is flatly illegal.

teaching.text: Plain brakes are pumped to stop a slide, bumpers sit higher as vehicles get heavier, and emission tampering is never allowed. Remember: Bumpers rise with weight.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Plain brakes pump sliding stops, bumpers step with weight, and emission tampering is flatly illegal.

question.text: How does lighting differ between light and heavy trailers?

answer.text: Light trailers reflector-pair while heavy ones lamp their corners and rears.

teaching.text: Light trailers rely on a pair of reflectors, while heavy trailers add lamps at their corners and rear. Remember: Reflectors light, lamps heavy.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Light trailers reflector-pair while heavy ones lamp their corners and rears.

question.text: What rules apply to towed brakes and trailer stop lamps?

answer.text: Towed brakes answer the driver and self-stop on breakaway, heavy pole trailers lamp and reflector both sides, and stop lamps run two except pre-nineteen seventy-two singles.

teaching.text: A towed vehicle's brakes must respond to the driver and stop it if it breaks loose, heavy pole trailers need lamps and reflectors on both sides, and stop lamps come in pairs except on older trailers. Remember: Breakaway brakes stop the trailer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Towed brakes answer the driver and self-stop on breakaway, heavy pole trailers lamp and reflector both sides, and stop lamps run two except pre-nineteen seventy-two singles.

question.text: What rules apply to drawbars and connecting chains?

answer.text: Drawbars must hold the load, span at most fifteen feet except for long objects, and flag chains and cables with a twelve-inch white square.

teaching.text: A drawbar must be strong enough for the load and no longer than fifteen feet except for long objects, and chains and cables carry a twelve-inch white square flag. Remember: Fifteen feet, flag the chain.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drawbars must hold the load, span at most fifteen feet except for long objects, and flag chains and cables with a twelve-inch white square.

question.text: How must loads be secured?

answer.text: Loads must never drop, shift, leak, or escape, loose hauls wear covers, and log trucks chain down.

teaching.text: Loads must never fall, shift, leak or escape, loose cargo must be covered, and log trucks must chain their loads. Remember: Nothing drops, shifts or leaks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Loads must never drop, shift, leak, or escape, loose hauls wear covers, and log trucks chain down.

question.text: How are long rear overhangs marked by day and night?

answer.text: Rear overhangs past four feet flag eighteen-inch red squares by day and lamp five hundred-foot reds with one hundred-to-six hundred-foot reflectors by night and rain, with log poles adding an always-on amber strobe.

teaching.text: Rear overhangs over four feet carry eighteen-inch red flags by day and red lamps with reflectors at night and in rain, and log poles add an amber strobe that stays on. Remember: Red flag day, red lamp night.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rear overhangs past four feet flag eighteen-inch red squares by day and lamp five hundred-foot reds with one hundred-to-six hundred-foot reflectors by night and rain, with log poles adding an always-on amber strobe.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Red flag day, red lamp night

question.text: How far may a load on a car extend to the sides?

answer.text: Car loads never pass the left fender line and pass the right by at most six inches.

teaching.text: Cargo on a car may never stick out past the left fender line and may go no more than six inches past the right one. Remember: Left fender line, right six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Car loads never pass the left fender line and pass the right by at most six inches.

question.text: What happens if a towed vehicle breaks away, and how many stop lamps are required?

answer.text: Towed brakes answer the driver and self-stop when parted, with stop lamps doubled except pre-nineteen seventy-two singles.

teaching.text: If a towed vehicle comes loose its brakes must stop it on their own, and it shows two stop lamps unless it is an older single-lamp trailer. Remember: Parted trailers stop themselves.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Towed brakes answer the driver and self-stop when parted, with stop lamps doubled except pre-nineteen seventy-two singles.

question.text: How long may a drawbar be, and how are loose loads handled?

answer.text: A drawbar or towing connection must be strong enough for all towed weight, measure at most fifteen feet unless towing poles, pipes, machinery, or other objects not easily dismounted, and carry a white flag at least twelve inches square when using chain, rope, or cable; loads that could fall or blow require a close-fitting cover, and log or pulpwood trucks require lock chains.

teaching.text: Drawbars stop at fifteen feet with flagged chains and cables, loose loads are covered, and logs are chained down. Remember: Cover loose loads.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A drawbar or towing connection must be strong enough for all towed weight, measure at most fifteen feet unless towing poles, pipes, machinery, or other objects not easily dismounted, and carry a white flag at least twelve inches square when using chain, rope, or cable; loads that could fall or blow require a close-fitting cover, and log or pulpwood trucks require lock chains.

question.text: How are four-foot rear overhangs marked?

answer.text: Loads extending past the sides and four feet or more past the rear need eighteen-inch-square red flags by day, and from sunset to sunrise or in rain, smoke, or fog require two rear red lamps visible five hundred feet, two rear red reflectors visible one hundred to six hundred feet, and red side clearance lamps visible five hundred feet; log, pulpwood, pole, or post loads overhanging past four feet always need an operating amber strobe visible from behind and both sides.

teaching.text: Overhangs longer than four feet get red flags in daylight and red lamps with reflectors at night, plus an amber strobe for log poles. Remember: Four feet means flag it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Loads extending past the sides and four feet or more past the rear need eighteen-inch-square red flags by day, and from sunset to sunrise or in rain, smoke, or fog require two rear red lamps visible five hundred feet, two rear red reflectors visible one hundred to six hundred feet, and red side clearance lamps visible five hundred feet; log, pulpwood, pole, or post loads overhanging past four feet always need an operating amber strobe visible from behind and both sides.

question.text: What side limits apply to loads on a car?

answer.text: Car loads hold the left fender line and clear the right by six inches at most.

teaching.text: Keep car loads inside the left fender line, and let them reach no more than six inches beyond the right one. Remember: Six inches past the right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Car loads hold the left fender line and clear the right by six inches at most.
